rows.description: A working adult keeps notes, reviews key skills at intervals, and treats forgetting as the mind's ordinary filtering rather than a sign of failing.

rows.description: A child who has moved schools remembers the old class as perfect and forgets the quarrels. Distance smooths rough edges of the past.

rows.description: A teenager feeling pressure remembers early childhood as carefree and longs for it, forgetting its fears and limits. Comfort and loss colour the picture.

rows.description: A student in a hostel far from home idealises home life and old friends, and may feel homesick with love mixed with a bit of avoidance of present challenges.

rows.description: A young professional hears elders praise the old days and notes the warm memory is real even if the past was harder than described. Listening kindly without arguing keeps bonds strong.

rows.description: A wise person enjoys nostalgia as comfort and a source of values, and reminds herself of what was also hard, so the past does not make the present seem poor.

rows.description: A child feeling upset remembers only bad things about the week and expects tomorrow to be bad too. Feelings pick what the mind recalls.

rows.description: A teenager in a low mood reads neutral messages as rejection and recalls only failures. Judgment feels like fact, though the mood is shaping it. Persistent low mood deserves caring adult attention and professional help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult in a great mood underestimates risks and says yes to too much. Joy, like sadness, tilts the thoughts that come to mind.

rows.description: A wise person notices her mood, postpones major choices and messages during anger or despair, and returns when calm to see whether the view has changed.
